slots.title: Trump targets offshore data center builds
slots.body:
President Trump said firms building data centers abroad could face a tax.

Coverage framed it at the intersection of politics and where AI infrastructure gets built.

On the prior close, the Nasdaq Composite was down 5.3% to 22,617.73.

The S&P 500 fell 3.7% to 6,910.39.

The CBOE Volatility Index rose 26.2% to 35.89.

How much does where a data center sits matter to you when you read headlines like this?

slots.title: S&P 6,910 after 3.7% session drop
slots.body:
The S&P 500 closed down 3.7% at 6,910.39.

Coverage put the index about 11.9% below its early-October high and down about 8.6% for the week.

The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.3% to 22,617.73.

That same coverage cited roughly a 10.0% Nasdaq decline for the week and said the index had wiped out the year’s gains.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 1.9%, finishing at 48,147.33.

The Russell 2000 was down 2.8% at 2,581.79.

What label do you use for a move like this — pullback, correction, or something else?

slots.title: U.S. cash session — Nov. 21, 2026
slots.body:
The Nasdaq Composite took the largest hit among major U.S. indexes, closing at 22,617.73 after a 1,261.47-point (-5.3%) drop.
The session low was 22,513.01.

The S&P 500 ended at 6,910.39, down 265.44 points (-3.7%), with an intraday low of 6,882.66.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average finished at 48,147.33 (-949.73, -1.9%).
The Russell 2000 closed at 2,581.79 (-2.8%).

The VIX closed at 35.89, up 7.45 (+26.2%) from the prior close of 28.44.
The index traded as high as 40.03, which matches the year high in the injected series.

Nvidia was among the most active issues and closed at 125.53 (-20.45, -14.0%).
Taiwan Semiconductor ended at 318.71 (-9.5%).
Oracle finished at 101.19 (-8.5%) with a session low of 100.28 at its year low.
ASML closed at 1,266.22 (-6.6%).
Intel ended at 51.28 (-8.0%).

Other megacap technology names declined in line with the Nasdaq: Tesla at 345.82 (-7.6%), Meta at 560.84 (-5.9%), Amazon at 246.82 (-4.1%), Apple at 342.56 (-1.9%), and Alphabet at 265.29 (-2.7%).
The bullish semiconductor ETF SOXL closed at 30.88 (-31.8%); bearish leveraged products such as SOXS rose 31.7% to 83.16.

A subset of consumer and staples names closed higher on the day: Walmart at 127.95 (+1.5%), Costco at 1,102.15 (+0.8%), Home Depot at 339.04 (+0.7%), PepsiCo at 140.54 (+1.1%), and Procter & Gamble at 169.37 (+0.9%).
Exxon Mobil rose 0.7% to 159.99.

Gold futures settled at 3,515.40, down 170.10 (-4.6%), with a session low of 3,502.90 at the year low in the injected commodity tape.
Bitcoin closed at 55,810.43 (-5.1%).
Brent crude was at 92.57 (+0.6%); the U.S. Oil Fund (USO) closed at 139.63 (+1.1%).

Overseas benchmarks in the feed were also lower before the U.S. close: the Nikkei 225 at 56,436.65 (-5.1%), Hang Seng at 22,410.80 (-3.8%), FTSE 100 at 10,346.34 (-1.0%), and the Germany proxy EWG at 39.17 (-2.5%).

The injected Treasury snapshot (dated 2026-11-19) showed the 10-year at 5.0% and the 2s10s spread at 0.28.
The economic and earnings calendars in the feed were empty for this package.

News items in the feed highlighted an accelerating AI-related equity selloff, multiple sectors in correction versus recent highs, and remarks that U.S. companies building data centers abroad could face a tax.

slots.title: Three PMI prints open the week Monday
slots.body:
Monday, Nov. 23, 9:45 a.m.
ET: S&P Global PMI suite for November.

Manufacturing PMI — prior print: 54.9 (above 50 means expansion).

Services PMI — prior: 56.1.

Composite PMI — prior: 55.9.

PMI is a survey of purchasing managers; the headline is a single number where 50 separates growth from contraction.

No consensus estimates are in this week’s calendar payload for these three lines.

Same day kicks off a shortened Thanksgiving week (through Nov. 27).

Earnings also on Monday include $HPE (EPS est.
$1.28), $ZM ($1.49), and $A ($1.73).
